payload.claim: `test_the_duplicated_agent_renderer_still_matches_its_original` used to compare two independently-maintained renderers (`implement._describe` vs `events._describe_agent_event`) and could fail if they diverged. After this diff it constructs `Agent(event=event)` and compares `_describe_agent_event(event)` to `describe(wrapped)` — but `describe()`'s own Agent branch, when `event.raw` is False and `event.event` is not None, does nothing but `return _describe_agent_event(event.event)`. The assertion is therefore `_describe_agent_event(event) == _describe_agent_event(event)`, which cannot fail regardless of what `_describe_agent_event` computes. Before this migration `Agent.event` was always `None` in production (the bug this spec fixes), so `_describe_agent_event` was effectively unreachable outside tests; after this migration it is the sole renderer for every real `agent:` line the operator and `events.jsonl` see, yet its `text`, `tool_result`, `result`, `rate_limit`, and unknown-kind fallback branches (unlike `tool_use`, `error`, and the raw/reap/pipe-closed lines, which do have literal-string assertions elsewhere in this file and in `test_the_watch_shaped_callable_phases_still_receive_does_not_raise`) now have no test anywhere that checks their rendered output against a hand-written expected string — the golden fixture explicitly excludes every `agent:` form. A future edit that silently breaks, say, the `rate_limit` or `result` line would pass every test in this file, including the one whose docstring claims to guarantee the renderer's behaviour.
